newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1996 coffee harvest similar to 1994 - CNC.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1996 coffee harvest similar to 1994 - CNC.

text.p: Brazil's National Coffee Council (CNC) believes the 1996/97 coffee crop was similar in size to the 26 million to 27 million 60-kg bags harvested in 1994/95, said an article in April's Garcafe bulletin.
The bulletin is produced by the Garca cooperative, whose president Manoel Bertone is vice-president of the growers' body.

According to CNC data, some 8.21 million bags of coffee were received by cooperatives between May 1996 and March 1997 against 6.12 million bags in a similar period in 1993/94 and 7.43 million bags in 1994/95.
"Given that many analysts link coffee received by cooperatives to the volume produced by Brazil, CNC directors carried out a detailed analysis of coffee received by its members," the article said.
The survey showed that the higher deliveries were due to associations contributing data for the first time to the CNC statistics, the article said.
"For this reason, the CNC continues to believe the harvest in 1996 was similar to that in 1994," the Garcafe article said.
The CNC estimate for the 1994 harvest is between 26 million to 27 million bags, Bertone said.
